entities.evidence: The verse names Jabal’s brother Jubal and identifies him as the father of those who play the lyre and pipe. The source tag at position 2 identifies the same musician.

review.translation: [And the name of|0] [his brother|1] {was} [Jubal|2]. [He|3] [was|4] [the father of|5] [all|6] [who play|7] [the lyre|8] [and pipe|9].

draft.change: Add Genesis 4:21 as an example of the existing identifying-name sense of שֵׁם.
draft.definition: The name by which a person is known.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:21 identifies the brother by giving his name, Jubal.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם אָחִיו means “his brother’s name.” The following יוּבָל supplies that name, so the clause reads “and his brother’s name was Jubal.”
analysis.morphology: Prefixed conjunction וְ (and) + masculine singular construct noun שֵׁם.
analysis.sense: name by which someone is known

analysis.evidence: וְשֵׁם אָחִיו יוּבָל means “and his brother’s name was Jubal.” The suffix refers to Jabal, introduced in the preceding verse, and יוּבָל names his brother.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: וְשֵׁם אָחִיו יוּבָל means “and his brother’s name was Jubal.” The following הוּא refers to Jubal and introduces him as the forefather of those who play the lyre and pipe.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In הוּא הָיָה אֲבִי, “he was the father of,” הוּא refers back to יוּבָל (Jubal) and serves as the subject of הָיָה, “was.”
analysis.morphology: Independent personal pronoun, third person masculine singular.

analysis.evidence: הוּא refers to Jubal. הָיָה links him to the predicate אֲבִי כָּל־תֹּפֵשׂ כִּנּוֹר וְעוּגָב, describing his role as the father of all who play the lyre and pipe.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: אֲבִי governs כָּל־תֹּפֵשׂ כִּנּוֹר וְעוּגָב, “everyone who plays the lyre and pipe.” The verse identifies Jubal as the father of a group defined by its craft, giving אָב the sense “founder.”
כָּל qualifies the singular participle תֹּפֵשׂ, “one who plays.” The phrase אֲבִי כָּל תֹּפֵשׂ כִּנּוֹר וְעוּגָב describes Jubal as the father of everyone who plays the lyre and pipe.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל תֹּפֵשׂ כִּנּוֹר וְעוּגָב means “everyone who plays the lyre and pipe.” The two instruments specify what the player handles.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular construct, used substantivally.
analysis.sense: handle a musical instrument in order to play it

analysis.evidence: In תֹּפֵשׂ כִּנּוֹר וְעוּגָב, the participle תֹּפֵשׂ governs two instruments, the lyre and the pipe. The phrase describes the musicians whose ancestor was Jubal.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute common noun, with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add עוּגָב with its instrumental sense under עגב. The source gloss ‘good pleasure; will’ does not fit the two objects of תֹּפֵשׂ.
draft.definition: A musical instrument, probably a pipe, played alongside the lyre.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:21 names the עוּגָב among the instruments handled by Jubal’s successors. Job 21:12 describes people rejoicing at its sound.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל תֹּפֵשׂ כִּנּוֹר וְעוּגָב, the conjunction places עוּגָב alongside the lyre as a second instrument that a musician handles. The verse establishes its use as an instrument but leaves its construction uncertain.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed conjunction וְ ‘and’ + masculine singular common noun in the absolute state.
analysis.sense: A musical instrument, probably a pipe.
